case_155.comparison: exact-rational componentwise error against exact decimal tolerances
case_155.label_scope: One fixed implementation under the complete finite-FP16 complex input contract.
case_155.analysis: Direct control has a source-bound whole-domain roundoff proof. Actual T4 checks use exact-rational references, random tuples, cancellation, component sweeps, extremes, tails, offsets, aliased inputs and guard preservation. Component sweeps do not enumerate all input tuples.

proof: Every finite binary16 value is an integer multiple of2^-24 and has at most11 significant binary bits. Its product with another binary16 value has at most22 significant bits, so conversion and product in FP32 are exact.

Every nonzero product is at least2^-48; all products have magnitude below2^32. A sum or difference of two products is either zero or at least2^-48, and its magnitude is below2^33. All exact and rounded nonzero products and sums are normal FP32 values; overflow and underflow do not occur.

For either component, write the exact numerator asP and the positive exact denominator asD. The direct kernel computes RN(RN(P)/RN(D)), with exactly formed products and with implicit FMA disabled. Thus the relative factor is(1+e1)*(1+e3)/(1+e2), where each|ei|<=u. A zeroP is computed exactly aszero.

The nonzero quotient's loose magnitude bounds2^-81 to2^81 remain inside the normal FP32 range, including the small roundoff factors. The maximum relative error is at most(1+u)^2/(1-u)-1<1.789e-7<5e-7. This proves the componentwise tolerance for every legal tuple, including severe cancellation.

The scalar proof is bound to the candidate source expressions. GPU tests check actual lowering, tails, offsets, input guards and separate storage; this is not a formal proof of all GPU execution behavior.

expressions.imag_numerator: tl.where(real_dominant, tl.fma(-a, ratio, b), tl.fma(b, ratio, -a))

cpu_audit.oracle: Exact arbitrary-precision rational components from integer-scaled FP16 values. Comparisons use exact rational error and exact decimal tolerances.
cpu_audit.indexing: Program p covers indices256*p through256*p+255 with index<N masks. Each legal index reads2components from each input and writes2distinct output components. Maximum offset262143 is int32-safe. Nonzero input storage offsets are incorporated by the tensor pointer.

structural_audit.scalar_correctness_argument: The int32 operands convert to int64 exactly. Product and positive bias stay within signed int64. Arithmetic right shift by 31+r is floor division by its positive power of two, and adding half that divisor before floor division implements nearest rounding with ties toward positive infinity, including negative products. Clipping R to [-255,255] before adding z in [-128,127] preserves final INT8 saturation and prevents narrow integer overflow.
structural_audit.address_argument: One-dimensional launch uses index=128*program+lane and mask index<M*C. Each active index has one unique output and input cell. Channel index=index%C is in [0,C). Read-only parameters can alias inputs. Relative pointer arithmetic is unchanged by legal storage offsets. Output is newly allocated and has no input alias.
structural_audit.scope: Full-domain source arithmetic and indexing argument, finite integer and compiled-GPU cross-checks. This is not a formal proof of the compiler or every GPU execution.
